chapters.title: The Old House
chapters.summary: Mara spends the entire chapter cataloguing the contents of her late aunt's house, room by room, listing furniture and old photographs. No new case information emerges and no character makes a decision.

chapters.title: The Reservoir
chapters.summary: A long, static chapter: Mara watches divers search the reservoir for hours; the narration dwells at length on the weather, the colour of the water, and her coffee going cold. The plot does not advance.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Sudden acceleration: a suspect confesses, a second body is found, and Mara is attacked, all in a few pages. The case breaks open.

plantedDefects.note: Chapters 2 and 3 are a clear mid-book pacing sag: two consecutive static chapters (house inventory, watching divers) that do not advance the plot, between a propulsive opening (ch1) and a rushed climax (ch4). The model should flag a pacing problem anchored in chapter 2 or 3 with verdict improve (tighten/cut the sag).

notes: Single dominant planted defect: a pacing sag in the middle. The synopsis/other dimensions are deliberately coherent so a precise reviewer surfaces pacing and little else.

chapters.title: The Funeral

chapters.summary: The siblings gather to read the will. Eldest sister Ruth recalls the funeral and the lawyer notes that probate began the week after the burial.

The model should flag a continuity finding anchored in chapter 3 (or spanning ch1+ch3), verdict improve (or cut the contradictory detail).

bookBrief.synopsis: When the old king dies without a clear heir, the bastard scholar Corwin is dragged into a succession war between three claimant houses, while his estranged sister Yara is named in a temple prophecy that no one will explain.

chapters.title: The King Is Dead

King Aldous dies in the opening pages and the capital, Vael, erupts into factional manoeuvring. We meet the three claimant houses and the shape of the succession crisis is laid out with dense, assured intelligence. Corwin's outsider position, inside the palace yet owning nothing, is established as the lens for the whole book, and the prose has a dry, watchful poise that will be the book's signature.
Plot events: Aldous dies without naming a clear heir; the three houses begin to position for the throne; Corwin is summoned to court to read the dynastic ledgers; Corwin is publicly acknowledged for the first time as the king's bastard.
Characters: Corwin: scholar-archivist, illegitimate, watchful and self-effacing, terrified of being used | Duke Tomas of House Renar: the dead king's brother, cold and ambitious, sees Corwin as a tool | Queen Iselle of House Sable: widowed regent for her infant son, pragmatic and dangerous | General Garran of House Voss: frontier commander with the army's loyalty, blunt and honourable.
Themes: the vacuum left by power, legitimacy and blood, the outsider as witness.
Open threads: who will take the throne; why Corwin specifically was summoned.
Tone: dry, watchful, assured; controlled court intelligence.

The central mystery crystallises and Corwin commits himself to it, knowing it makes him a target.

A MAJOR SECONDARY THREAD opens here with enormous weight. chapters.summary:
רונית ואבי מתפייסים בהדרגה ובזהירות, וסצנת הפיוס חמה ומרפאת, מבלי למחוק את הכאב שקדם לה. הספר ממשיך להחזיק את הקול האנושי-החומל שלו לכל אורכו עד כה, אחת-עשרה פרקים של עדינות עקבית. המשבר הזוגי נפתר לא בניצחון של צד אחד אלא בהבנה הדדית. הכתיבה רכה, בוגרת, ומלאת אמונה ביכולתם של אנשים פגועים לתקן.

chapters.title: טיפול
chapters.summary:
מזל מתחילה טיפול במחלתה, והפרק מלווה את המשפחה בתקווה זהירה ובשגרה החדשה של ימי הטיפול. הטון נשאר עדין ומלא חיבה: יש פחד, אך יש גם הומור וקרבה. אזכור קצר של חוט הבעל הנעלם, כשרונית מציינת בצער שעדיין אין שום חדשות על בעלה של גברת אזולאי. הכתיבה ממשיכה למצוא אור גם בתוך הקושי, נאמנה לרוח הספר.

chapters.title: יום הולדת
chapters.summary:
יום הולדת לאחד הנכדים, וחגיגה קטנה ומאולתרת בחצר המשותפת היא רגע של אור לפני הסיבוב האחרון של הספר. הטון החם נמצא בשיאו האחרון: בלונים, עוגה, שירה, והסבתא מזל מחייכת מתוך עייפותה. הכתיבה מצוינת ומלאת חסד, וחותמת אחת-עשרה פרקים רצופים של קול חומל, עדין ואנושי. זהו הרגע האחרון שבו הספר עדיין נאמן לחלוטין לרוחו המקורית.

chapters.summary:

_note: SMALL book with a SUBTLE single defect (wb2-c06): a protagonist whose interior changes not at all across four chapters that all gesture at transformation - a flat character arc. Designed to break the 100% ceiling: there is no dramatic event to flag, only the ABSENCE of growth, which a surface reviewer misses.

bookBrief.synopsis: A reclusive piano tuner is given a year of chances to change his life and, beneath a surface of incident, changes nothing at all.

chapters.title: Spring
chapters.summary: Martin, a solitary piano tuner, is introduced through his fixed daily routine. A new client, the warm and curious Dr. Okafor, invites him to a recital and gently challenges his isolation. The chapter clearly FRAMES the book as a transformation story: the premise, the title structure (seasons), and Dr. Okafor's role all promise that Martin will change. Martin is intrigued but declines. Well-written, controlled.

chapters.title: Summer
chapters.summary: Martin has more encounters that invite change: an old friend reappears, the recital invitation is renewed, a chance at companionship opens. On the SURFACE the chapter is full of incident and 'almost' moments. But Martin's interior is described in exactly the same terms as chapter 1 - the same guarded thoughts, the same retreat to routine, the same justifications. He declines again, in the same way. The prose is lovely and the events imply movement, but the character does not actually shift.

chapters.title: Autumn
chapters.summary: The pattern repeats with new surface events: a small crisis at a concert hall, Dr. Okafor's persistence, a near-confession. Each is set up as the turning point. Yet Martin's reflections, fears, and choices are again identical in substance to chapters 1-2; the narration even reuses the same interior images (the locked room, the cold tea). The book keeps PROMISING an arc and keeps not delivering one, but the repetition is quiet enough to read as 'style' rather than as a flaw.

chapters.title: Winter
chapters.summary: The year closes. The seasonal structure and the recurring cast all signal that this is where Martin finally changes. There is a last invitation. Martin declines once more and returns to his unchanged routine; the final image mirrors the first almost exactly. The book PRESENTS this as a poignant resolution, but Martin has had no genuine internal development across the four chapters despite the structure repeatedly promising one - a flat protagonist arc masquerading as a completed one.

plantedDefects.note: SUBTLE FLAT CHARACTER ARC: the book's structure (seasons, a transformation premise, a catalyst character) repeatedly PROMISES that Martin will change, but his interior, fears, and choices are essentially identical across all four chapters - the arc is flat while pretending to complete. There is no single dramatic defect to point at; the flaw is the ABSENCE of development, visible only by comparing the protagonist's interior across the whole book. The model should flag a character (or plot) finding about the flat/unfulfilled arc, anchored late (ch3 or ch4; leniency covers it), verdict improve.
